newsitem.title: UK: Airbus may offer foreign firms share in A3XX.
newsitem.headline: Airbus may offer foreign firms share in A3XX.

text.p: Europe's Airbus Industrie is likely to offer a one-third share in its new A3XX superjumbo plane to foreign firms to help finance the project, a senior member of the four-nation consortium said.
Sir Richard Evans, chief executive of Airbus partner British Aerospace, said there had been some hope that foreign participation could be brought in to cover 40 percent of the project.

"Realistically I think that number is going to be closer to 30 percent," he told Reuters at the Farnborough air show. "That will leave the partners with 70 percent of the project to finance themselves."

Airbus has identified potential partners in Singapore, China, Japan and north America but Evans said the consortium still had to finalise the aircraft's design with airlines before it could start actively seeking industrial partners.
"And that process is not likely to be completed until next spring," he said.

Airbus says it needs the large aircaft to challenge Boeing Co's lucrative monopoly of the 747 jumbo jet market and its plans to develop a stretched version of the 747-400 with 25 percent more capacity than the 425-seat aircraft.
Boeing's new 747-600X could be ready for first deliveries by the year 2000 if it can get launch orders confirmed by the end of this year.
Airbus says its superjumbo could be ready to go into service by the year 2003 and later versions could take up to 990 passengers in a double-decker configuration.
Evans said the 2003 date was feasible and there was nothing in practice to halt the development of a superjumbo.
He said that with take-off and landing slots so difficult to come by at major airports, the only answer was to create larger aircraft to cope with future demand.
The Farnborough air show, held every two years, has attracted a record 1,164 exhibitors from 60 nations.
